verified_behaviors: X-Gitlab-Token is compared in constant time against PARALLAX_GITLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
a missing or wrong token is rejected with 401 before the payload is parsed
an empty secret disables the endpoint with 404 instead of accepting anything
X-Gitlab-Event must be Merge Request Hook and object_kind must be merge_request
open/reopen/update actions create a review task; other actions return not-accepted
project.git_http_url must match the registered clone URL of the linked repository
the numeric GitLab project id must resolve to an explicit GITLAB repository link
the task uses the latest immutable policy and the fixed object_attributes.last_commit.id
X-Gitlab-Event-UUID provides idempotent task creation (same task on replay)
reusing an event UUID with a different payload is rejected with 409
GitHub and GitLab share one acceptance path, so both persist delivery id, payload digest, MR number, repository and task id
the disabled system.webhook account remains the task author and each delivery is audited
limitations: A real GitLab merge-request hook delivery has not been performed; it needs a public HTTPS endpoint
GitLab does not sign the body, so the shared token is the only sender authentication
The webhook secret is deployment-wide; per-tenant secrets are pending
Push hooks and merge-result pipelines are intentionally ignored
